name: Residence -- Grandchild of a Person Born in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

qualifying_event.description: Grandchildren of persons born in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines may apply for residency (distinct from citizenship) on the strength of that ancestry.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Birth and marriage certificates proving the relationship to the Vincentian-born grandparent(s).

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must be the grandchild of a person born in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, proven via official birth and marriage certificates establishing the relationship.

evidence_required.document: Grandparent's birth certificate (born in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines)
Chain of birth/marriage certificates linking applicant to that grandparent

sources.title: High Commission for Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, UK -- Non-National: confirms grandchildren of persons born in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines may apply for residency on proof of the relationship, but no further criteria, duration, or fee detail is given

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' initial build. STATUS: DRAFT -- extremely thin sourcing (a single confirming sentence on an official diplomatic-mission page, no further detail found anywhere else). This is a RESIDENCE route, explicitly distinct from vc_citizenship_by_descent.json's second-generation citizenship registration ground (which was amended into the Citizenship Act via the 2023 Amendment Bill and reaches the same grandparent-tie population) -- the two may function as alternative options for the same applicant (faster/cheaper residency here vs. full citizenship registration there), similar to the marriage-vs-PR distinction flagged in Grenada's build, but this is not explicitly confirmed by any source and is flagged as an inference about how the two tracks likely relate rather than a stated rule.
